A1.justification: Both complete 19-page PDFs describe the same work and include Appendices A–D. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical content except for the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original transformer-training, representation-probing, relational-algebra and model-editing experiments in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The GPT-NeoX architecture, three relational probes, objectives, SVD-based relation-matrix update and layer-wise editing procedure are identical.

E1.justification: Both use the same synthetic family dataset with eight relations, withheld father/mother prediction tasks and logically related model-editing evaluations.

E2.justification: The same linear, translational and bilinear probes and reversal-cursed/non-cursed model groups participate in the corresponding comparisons. No evaluated comparator changes.

E3.justification: Data splits, model configurations, training budgets, weight-decay sweeps, probing sample sizes and editing evaluation procedures and metrics are unchanged in Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–D.

E4.justification: Both retain the same regularization analysis, inversion/composition tests, probing sample-size comparison, per-relation analyses and layer-wise editing analyses, including Appendix D.

E5.justification: Both report three training seeds per weight-decay setting and means over 50 independent edits. Plotted uncertainty and statistical reporting are identical.

E6.justification: All reported values and result curves in Figures 2–11 match, including 100% direct-edit accuracy and the bilinear-accuracy/editing-generalization association with R² = 0.939.

T1.justification: The probe definitions and objectives in Section 4.2 and the SVD update derivation and computational-complexity reasoning in Appendix C are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims connecting bilinear representations with overcoming the reversal curse and logically consistent model editing.

C2.justification: Sections 4.4–5 retain the same interpretation of editing layers, discussion of unintended edit propagation and limitations concerning synthetic data and applicability to large pretrained models.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement and Appendices A–D preserve the same hardware, hyperparameters, dataset-generation instructions and implementation details. Access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the references and the claimed positioning relative to prior reversal-curse, relational-representation and model-editing research are identical.

P1.justification: Only the marginal arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 26 September 2025 to v2 dated 7 November 2025. Prose, terminology, headings and document structure remain identical.

P2.justification: All 11 figures, their captions, axes, legends and placement are identical. Rendered pages show no layout changes beyond the version/date text update.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, supporting evidence, appendices and presentation are unchanged. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp provides no meaningful improvement or deterioration in paper quality.
